author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its recorded name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name, all on one page. It is reached by its address alone; no navigation entry or link leads to it.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it.
Each veterinarian under a specialty is shown by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
All specialties render on one page; the page offers no paging.
Edge case 3: a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them.
Edge case 4: a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, shown as held by none rather than left blank.
Edge case 5: specialties appear in alphabetical order by name; under each specialty, veterinarians appear in alphabetical order by last name, then first name.
Per REQ-LANG-002, the page's own wording (heading, labels, the held-by-none marker) is present in every supported language; specialty and veterinarian names are shown as recorded, untranslated.
Per REQ-SYS-001, the page carries the site navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory; the navigation gains no entry for the specialty directory.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged by the owner's intake decision).
Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory (owner decision; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request, recorded in PRD Open Questions).
Searching or filtering veterinarians or specialties on the page (NG-9: only owners are searchable).
A machine-readable form of the specialty directory (the machine-readable veterinarian list, REQ-VET-002, is withdrawn as unconsumed).
Any change to the existing veterinarian directory's behavior (REQ-VET-001).
notes: Grounded in intake-decision line 1. Boundary check: no contradiction with a recorded requirement or Non-Goals row; no Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Reversible decisions taken per the narrowest-reading instruction: edge case 4 (unheld specialty listed and marked held by none, mirroring REQ-VET-001) and edge case 5 (alphabetical ordering, needed for a testable stable order). Open question recorded in docs/prd.md: a visible entry point. No new domain term resolved at intake; ubiquitous language unchanged. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet-package patterns with one small adjustment: the inverse grouping and both orderings live in a new immutable value object, SpecialtyDirectory, never in the controller or template (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller and Value object rows; § Design Validation Checklist, no business rule in a web controller). The rest mirrors adjacent seams. SpecialtyRepository follows the lookup-value repository shape of PetTypeRepository and the narrow Repository interface of VetRepository. SpecialtyController follows VetController. The template follows vets/vetList.html. system-design.md updated: Contracts rows (three new contracts; REQ-VET-003 joins Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, CacheConfiguration), the Contracts invariants paragraph, the vet line of Package Structure, and a provenance exception marking the REQ-VET-003 statements as designed. No ADR: the inverse is derived in memory rather than by a new mapping, a choice this slice contains. Covering symbols confirmed by grep and source read (weaker basis, IDE oracle not connected): VetRepository.findAll() cached as 'vets'; Vet.getSpecialties() sorts on the model; BaseEntity declares no equals/hashCode; PetTypeRepository extends JpaRepository with an ORDER BY query.
integration_points: SpecialtyDirectory: immutable value object in the vet package, built by a static factory from the full specialty collection and the veterinarian collection. Entries carry plain values, not entity references: each specialty's recorded name, then for each veterinarian holding it the first and last name. Nested record names come from ubiquitous-language.md terms (architecture-principles.md § Domain Core; § Naming). It imports no infrastructure type.

SpecialtyRepository: extends Spring Data Repository<Specialty, Integer>, not JpaRepository, and declares only findAll() with @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable, matching VetRepository. No ORDER BY: ordering belongs to SpecialtyDirectory alone. CacheConfiguration is unchanged (architecture-principles.md § Design Principles 5, minimal surface).

SpecialtyController: package-private @Controller in the vet package, GET /specialties.html. It reads SpecialtyRepository.findAll() and the unpaged VetRepository.findAll(), builds SpecialtyDirectory, adds it as one model attribute, and returns the view name. It holds no loop, sort, or filter (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).

Binding per entry point: GET /specialties.html binds no request parameter and no model attribute. A supplied page parameter is ignored, because the page offers no paging. SpecialtyController still declares an @InitBinder disallowing "id" and "*.id" (security-principles.md § Realization, mass-assignment row: a new controller that omits the disallow list fails).

View: vets/specialtyDirectory.html through fragments/layout. It passes a menu key that no nav item carries, so the navigation gains no entry and none shows active (REQ-SYS-001; PRD non-goal on entry points). Full name is composed in the template as firstName + ' ' + lastName, as in vetList.html. Output uses th:text only (security-principles.md § Realization, XSS row).

Wording: the heading, labels, and held-by-none marker come from message keys. Reuse the existing specialties, vets, and none keys where the wording fits; any new key lands in all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/ (REQ-LANG-002; I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces both halves).
Double per boundary, framework transport: SpecialtyControllerTests is @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) driven by MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy).

Double per boundary, repositories in the web test: hand-written in-memory implementations of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository registered as beans through a nested @TestConfiguration, with no @MockitoBean. Both interfaces declare only their read methods, so a hand double is a few lines (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy, hand-write mocks).

Unit boundary: SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a plain JUnit test with no Spring context and no doubles. It uses real Vet and Specialty instances built behind test factory methods (testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction, Factory Methods; § Three-Tier Data Naming).

Exposed surface: one read-only GET that shows specialty names and veterinarian names already public on /vets.html. It discloses nothing new and mutates nothing (security-principles.md § Realization, widening-the-exposed-surface row).

patterns.description: Narrow Spring Data Repository interface with a read-only transactional findAll; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it, minus the cache
One repository per persisted lookup value; precedent for Specialty getting its own repository
getSpecialties() orders on the model, not in the controller (REQ-VET-001 edge case 1); SpecialtyDirectory keeps ordering on the model side the same way
showVetList: model attribute plus view-name return; the shape SpecialtyController follows, without pagination
Layout fragment use, first-then-last full-name composition, and the #{none} marker for an empty specialty list

risks.risk: Reference-equality trap. BaseEntity declares no equals/hashCode. Veterinarians come from the 'vets' cache and specialties from a fresh query, so one specialty exists as two distinct instances, and grouping by object or Set membership silently lists every specialty as held by none.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory pairs a veterinarian's specialties with the listed specialties by persisted id (architecture-principles.md § Domain Core: reference by identity; system-design.md Contracts invariants). SpecialtyDirectoryTests includes a case where the holder's Specialty and the listed Specialty are distinct instances sharing an id. Web-test doubles that share instances cannot catch this.

risks.risk: Mutating the cached veterinarian collection or its Vet entities while grouping or sorting would corrupt the shared 'vets' cache that REQ-VET-001 also reads.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory copies its inputs, never sorts or modifies a passed collection or entity in place, and exposes only unmodifiable lists (architecture-principles.md § Domain Core: defensive copies; system-design.md VetRepository row).

risks.risk: Grouping, filtering, or ordering drifting into the controller stream or into Thymeleaf sorting widens the controller-rule gap and pushes a unit-testable rule up the pyramid.
risks.mitigation: All three decisions live in SpecialtyDirectory and are unit-tested there; the web test asserts the rendered result only (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid).

risks.risk: Adding a bidirectional veterinarians association on Specialty to query the inverse would put a cycle into the serialized /vets output, changing the existing veterinarian routes.
risks.mitigation: Vet and Specialty mappings stay unchanged; the inverse is derived in memory (PRD non-goal: no change to REQ-VET-001 behavior; system-design.md § Persistence).

risks.risk: The unpaged page has no size bound.
risks.mitigation: Accepted by REQ-VET-003 (all specialties on one page). Specialty and veterinarian rows change only out of band, with no write path in the application (PRD NG-2; system-design.md Open Question 5).

notes: Test placement per testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid. In SpecialtyDirectoryTests (unit): theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListNoVeterinarianWhoHoldsNoSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyTheyHold, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderSpecialtiesByNameAndVeterinariansByLastThenFirstName, plus the identity-pairing case and an unheld specialty listed with no veterinarians. In SpecialtyControllerTests (web): theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredNameWithItsVeterinarians, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowEachVeterinarianByFirstThenLastName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderEverySpecialtyOnOnePageWithoutPaging, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarianAsHeldByNone (renders the marker), and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryTheSiteNavigation. The prd-entry file_targets name VetControllerTests. This design places the new page's web tests in a new SpecialtyControllerTests, one controller per HTTP surface, and leaves VetController and VetControllerTests untouched (REQ-VET-001 unchanged). Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Brief observations, not blocking: (1) the security-principles.md mass-assignment row, read literally, binds every new controller, including one that binds nothing; it is applied as written here. (2) The system-design.md Threat Model mass-assignment mitigation overstated coverage, since VetController, WelcomeController, and CrashController declare no binder; it now scopes to owner-feature controllers, still a derived statement. (3) 'Specialty directory' is a PRD page term, and the code type takes its name, but it is not in ubiquitous-language.md. The product-requirements-expert may add it.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: XSS: every record-derived value in templates/vets/specialtyDirectory.html goes out through escaped th:text (line 18 `th:text="${specialty.specialtyName}"`, line 21 `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}"`). A grep of the four changed production files for `utext|__\$\{|href|<script` found nothing (exit 1). So there is no unescaped output, no Thymeleaf preprocessing and no inline script or link.

Mass assignment: the new controller follows the project default from security-principles.md. SpecialtyController.java:44 reads `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");`, the same as OwnerController.java:61, VisitController.java:53 and PetController.java:91/97 (grep -F setDisallowedFields). The handler binds no request input: the same grep for `@ModelAttribute|@RequestBody|@RequestParam|@PathVariable` found nothing.

Injection: data access goes only through a derived Spring Data method (SpecialtyRepository.java:35 `Collection<Specialty> findAll() throws DataAccessException;`, `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`) and the existing cached VetRepository.findAll. The grep for `@Query|createQuery|nativeQuery|Runtime|ProcessBuilder|exec(|Files.` found nothing in the changed files.

Least privilege and cache integrity: the repository only reads, and the handler is GET-only (SpecialtyController.java:47 `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")`). The model carries immutable name-only records (SpecialtyDirectory.java:31/68/84), never the cached Vet entities, so rendering cannot mutate the shared `vets` cache.

Exposed surface: the new route exposes only specialty names and veterinarian first and last names, which the existing /vets.html and /vets routes already serve to any caller, so it is no weaker than the baseline. The unpaged findAll reads a lookup table that no route writes, plus the cached vet collection /vets already returns whole. The PRD (REQ-VET-003) and system-design Contracts row state what the route exposes. The layout's `__${link}__` preprocessing (fragments/layout.html:31) takes only fixed menu literals, and the new page passes the fixed menu name 'specialties', not request text.

Threat-model edit: the mass-assignment row now scopes its claim to 'Every owner-feature controller's data binder'. That corrects an overstatement, because VetController.java has no @InitBinder (grep -F setDisallowedFields lists no VetController hit). The new controller carries the disallow list anyway.

Secrets: the grep of the changed production files for `password|secret|token` found nothing. There are no log statements or System.out calls, and the change adds no new exception message that could reach the error page.

Supply chain: build.gradle and pom.xml are unchanged (git status --short shows nothing). `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` resolves spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.5. No dependencyCheckAnalyze task is configured (a grep of `./gradlew tasks --all` found none), so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: change-grader
summary: add the read-only specialty directory page

blast_radius.note: Additive and contained: three new package-private types in the vet package, one new template, and two new test files. No existing production file is edited, and the doc edits add rows plus one narrowed threat-model sentence. SpecialtyController is flagged as security surface, but it is a GET that shows specialty and veterinarian names /vets.html already serves.

semantic_surprise.note: Read in full, the code does what the PRD says. SpecialtyDirectory pairs specialties by persisted id, not by instance (the cache-versus-query trap the design named). It copies names out of the cached Vet entities and never mutates them (Vet.getSpecialties returns a fresh sorted list). Both orderings live in the record constructors. The template passes a menu key no nav item carries and uses th:text only. Residual edges that do not bite on seeded data: the name sort is case-sensitive, and two null ids would pair.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes. Whole-record equality covers multi-holder, non-holder, unheld-specialty, ordering, input non-mutation, and the distinct-instance id pairing. The web test's hand doubles build fresh instances on every call, and its paged findAll throws, which proves the page is unpaged. It also checks the held-by-none marker and that the nav has no entry or active item. A broken grouping or ordering would fail.

reviewer_hedging.note: The security reviewer's approval rests on SpecialtyController.java:44 carrying setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"). The fix round removed that binder, and the citation no longer resolves: the file is 45 lines, and grep finds no InitBinder in the vet package. The round-2 plan re-dispatched only code-quality, so no one re-reviewed the security aspect the approval cited. The test-reviewer's duplicated-factory recommendation is minor polish.

scope_deviation.note: The feature surface matches the PRD, but the fix round reversed a recorded design decision. The design block required the id disallow-list binder on this controller, citing docs/security-principles.md:34 ('A new controller or binder that omits the disallow list fails'). A code-quality autofix removed it as speculative generality. No consultation-response or revised design-block records that override of a written security rule.

rationale: The feature code is correct, contained, and genuinely tested. But the fix round removed the id disallow-list binder that security-principles.md:34 and the design block both require, with no recorded override, and the security approval still cites the deleted line. Decide whether the rule or the removal stands before merging.
